discrepancies_severity_ordered.finding: `axc rewrite-verify --kernel K --size N` (the `--size` convenience-shortcut path) does not actually work on a genuinely multi-kernel source, regardless of what `--kernel` is set to. `resolve_size_shortcut` in crates/axc-driver/src/main.rs (the CLI-level function that expands `--size N` into per-buffer sizes) calls the OLD kernel-agnostic `axc_driver::compile_source_with_assignments` and never receives the `kernel` selector at all -- so on any 2+-kernel source it always fails closed with AmbiguousKernel, even when `--kernel` correctly names one of the kernels. This is NOT a silent-wrong-answer bug (it fails closed, matching the project's fail-closed discipline) and the explicit `--buffer-sizes` path (bypassing `--size`) DOES correctly honor `--kernel` (independently reproduced: PASS verdict, correct kernel_name on both sides). But it is a real functional gap in the milestone's own promise ('Add --kernel NAME (applies to both original & rewritten sides)' for rewrite-verify), it was not caught by the coder's own test suite because AT-2963's tests call the library `verify_rewrite` function directly with an explicit `buffer_sizes` vector, never exercising the CLI's `--size` shortcut, and the milestone's own AT table marks AT-2963 as verified via 'CLI/integration' when the actual test is unit-level only. Recommend: either thread `kernel` into `resolve_size_shortcut` (and its one call site) in a small follow-up, or explicitly document `--size` as `--buffer-sizes`-only for multi-kernel sources.
discrepancies_severity_ordered.does_this_block_merge: No -- fails closed, no correctness risk, narrow CLI-convenience-flag gap, easily fixed in a follow-up patch.
